Definition: {something to sieze with, i.e. a finger; by analogy, a toe}
BiblicalUsage: ʼEtsbaʻ is a finger — or a toe, the thing you seize with. It turns up in Daniel: the toes of the king's image, part iron and part clay, and the fingers of a man's hand writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast. It is the word for the small, decisive thing.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from ʼetsbaʻ is straightforward: God writes with a finger, and the empires it touches fall. I hold that the small, decisive thing is the one to watch — the finger on the wall, the toe of iron and clay.
RelatedEvents: Nebuchadnezzar's Dream of the Image; Belshazzar's Handwriting on the Wall
